definitions.explanation: A prolonged duration of time, often used in contexts of planning, investment, or stays.

examples.japanese: {長期|ちょうき}{計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てる。
{長期|ちょうき}の{休暇|きゅうか}を{取|と}りたい。
examples.english: I want to take a long vacation.

examples.japanese: この{投資|とうし}は{長期|ちょうき}で{考|かんが}えるべきだ。
examples.english: This investment should be considered in the long term.

notes:
{長期|ちょうき} refers to an extended period, typically months to years. It functions as a noun and as a no-adjective modifier ({長期|ちょうき}の).

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {長期|ちょうき}{計画|けいかく} (long-term plan)
- {長期|ちょうき}{滞在|たいざい} (long stay, extended stay)
- {長期|ちょうき}{休暇|きゅうか} (long vacation)
- {長期|ちょうき}{投資|とうし} (long-term investment)
- {長期|ちょうき}{金利|きんり} (long-term interest rate)
- {長期|ちょうき}{戦|せん} (prolonged battle/struggle)

USAGE PATTERNS:
- {長期|ちょうき}にわたる (extending over a long period)
- {長期|ちょうき}{的|てき}に (in the long run)
- {長期|ちょうき}で{考|かんが}える (to think long-term)

TIME SCALE SERIES:
- {短期|たんき}: short-term (days to weeks)
- {中期|ちゅうき}: medium-term
- {長期|ちょうき}: long-term (months to years)
